sessions.title: Registration & Welcome Coffee
sessions.description: Welcome reception with refreshments and networking opportunities. Collect your conference materials and connect with fellow delegates.

sessions.title: Opening Ceremony & Keynote Address
sessions.description: Welcome addresses from co-organizers, Indigenous acknowledgment, and keynote on cultural resilience and care transformation in the 21st century.

sessions.title: Plenary Panel: Bridging Culture, Care & Climate
sessions.description: Global leaders discuss integrating cultural perspectives into climate action and care industry transformation.

sessions.title: Parallel Thematic Workshops: Culture & Care Integration
sessions.description: Deep-dive sessions on Climate Justice, Culture-Based Trade, and Cultural Approaches to Care.

sessions.title: Community Roundtables: Care for Caregivers
sessions.description: Grassroots leaders share community-led resilience initiatives and cultural heritage perspectives on care.

sessions.title: Plenary: Indigenous Knowledge & Care Systems
sessions.description: Indigenous leaders present traditional knowledge as solutions to contemporary care and environmental challenges.

sessions.title: Parallel Workshops: Redefining Care Industry
sessions.description: Sessions on Cultural Transformative Values for Care, Senior Participation in Decision-Making, and Technology Integration.

sessions.title: Youth Forum: Next Generation Leadership in Care
sessions.description: Young leaders present innovative approaches to cultural resilience and care transformation.

sessions.title: Research Presentations: Culture Meets Care
sessions.description: Academic and community researchers share findings on cultural approaches to care industry innovation.

sessions.title: Optional: Working Group Sessions
sessions.description: Final collaborative sessions for action planning and commitments.

sessions.title: Sydney Cultural & Tourism Experience
sessions.description: Guided tours of Sydney's iconic landmarks: Opera House, Harbour Bridge, Royal Botanic Gardens, and cultural sites. Experience Australia's vibrant multicultural heritage.

sessions.title: Optional: Sunset Harbour Cruise
sessions.description: Relaxing cruise on Sydney Harbour with networking opportunities.

sessions.title: Farewell Dinner (Optional)
sessions.description: Closing celebration with Australian cuisine and cultural performances.

venue.text: Sydney Showground is one of Australia's premier event destinations, located in Homebush Bay, Sydney. The Dome is a world-class, flexible venue capable of hosting large-scale international conferences, exhibitions, and cultural events.
venue.text3: Sydney Showground acknowledges the traditional custodians of the land and waters on which we meet. We pay our respects to Elders past and present.

openingCeremonyAndKeynoteSpeaker.label: Day 1 — 09:00 - 10:30
openingCeremonyAndKeynoteSpeaker.heading: Opening Ceremony & Keynote Speaker
openingCeremonyAndKeynoteSpeaker.text4: Brad Robinson is the CEO of Thrive Tours and a Haudenosaunee leader from Oneida Nation of the Thames. Under his leadership, Thrive Tours earned sustainability recognition at every level in 2025, internationally from the Indigenous Tourism Association of Canada and, weeks apart, provincially and nationally with the Sustainable Tourism Award from the Tourism Industry Association of Ontario and the Tourism Industry Association of Canada. In 2026, Thrive Tours was named a Sustainable Tourism Global Winner for Authenticity and Eco Adventure at Global Islands: Leading Beyond 2030 in Madeira, Portugal.
openingCeremonyAndKeynoteSpeaker.text5: As CROP 2026's Canadian anchor partner and Cultural Programming Lead, Brad brings two decades of Indigenous tourism and facilitation work to the gathering. His keynote will explore how Indigenous knowledge systems can inform global approaches to cultural resilience, care transformation, and planetary stewardship.

items5.desc: A pioneering organization dedicated to bridging cultural communities with sustainable development initiatives, redefining cultural understanding of care among Indigenous communities.

items5.name: Thrive Tours
items5.desc: Thrive Tours is a 100% Indigenous-owned and led experiential tourism and education company, headquartered at Batchewana First Nation in Bawaating (Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario, Canada). Haudenosaunee-led and working in respectful partnership with Anishinaabe Knowledge Carriers on whose territory it operates, Thrive Tours is among Canada’s most recognized Indigenous tourism companies, honoured for sustainability at the international, national, and provincial levels.
